u01-rem-early.resolution: Checked every flag against the Greek; none is a meaning error. Most are aspect/syntax style (aorist participles σοφίσαντα, σώσαντα, ἐπιφανείς, κροτήσασα rendered as relative or finite clauses; οὐ μήν as 'not'; Ἄρον 'lift up'). τῶν ἀσωμάτων 'the bodiless (ones)' is the standard Byzantine designation of the angels, so 'King of the angels' and 'chorus of the angels' keep the referent. θέανδρος against χήρανδρος is the wordplay 'no longer husbandless but with God as husband', which the English keeps. Ps 117:27 (118:27) is LXX numbering followed by English numbering, as the model concedes. μηδαμοῦ 'nowhere' as 'whom no place contains' keeps the meaning. None of the four phrases fixed in this pass (θύγατερ Θεοῦ, ἀγεωργήτως καὶ ἀνορύκτως, the nations once wild beasts, the first-person plural of κατέχοντες) is flagged as a meaning error; the 'of us' flag ignores that κατέχοντες is first-person plural.

u01-rem-early.resolution: Not meaning errors. ἀσωμάτων = the bodiless powers, conventionally the angels (see the kimi resolution). προαιώνιος 'pre-eternal' rendered 'eternal': same referent (the Son before the ages); a nuance, not a reversal, noted as an optional polish. Ἑόρταζε ἑορτάς is a cognate accusative, idiomatically 'keep the feast'. θέανδρος here answers χήρανδρος ('husbandless'), so 'with God as your husband' is the intended sense, not 'divine-human'. Chunks 3 and 5 pass.
